items.body: Refs #13766 (follow-up of #11185; does not close it — the attested-only preset itself is the next slice). ## Summary Settles publication-design §8.1 (exact body bytes of `attestation.claim`): the #6045 batch statement as a typed, canonical, digest-addressed record in `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/attestation.rs` — the attestation-marked claim shape the attested-only view preset keys on. - `BatchStatement`: in-toto Statement v1 (`_type`, `predicateType` `https://atlas.local/ingestBatch/v1`), `subject[]` chunk/span rows, `materials[]` source bytes with verbatim #6044 marks, `predicate.{builder, batch, classification, prior_attestation}` per #6045 §2. - `canonical_bytes()`: keys sorted at every depth (existing `canonical_json`); `envelope_digest()` is sha256 of those bytes — the attestation's primary key and the `prior_attestation` chain link. `from_canonical_bytes()` only accepts canonical bytes (reordered, pretty-printed, or duplicate-key spellings refused). - `to_envelope()`: DSSE envelope, `signatures: []` in v1 (signing optional, #6045 §6). - A rejected batch seals with an empty `subject[]`; validation fails closed on wrong type URIs and malformed digests. Shape only: no `ingest_attestations` table, no gate wiring, no projector mapping — those are later slices. The projector (#11183) consumes `canonical_bytes()` as the `attestation.claim` body bytes. Also records the predicate decision on #13766 (comment): a published version is attested iff a `tag.set` claim named `atlas.wasGeneratedBy` names it as subject and values an `attestation.claim` whose body is one of these statements. The preset could not be a pure view yet: the projection layer sees only `SnapshotEvent { kind, subject, deps }`, and tag-claim names/values live in event bodies the snapshot does not carry. ## Evidence Remote verification via the `fleet-command.yml` workflow fallback (`fleet queue dispatch` is blocked by TLS defect #13185 — `invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer`): - First run https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45283978459 failed on one compile error (E0382: proptest moved `statement` before `envelope_digest()`); fixed in a592ef291. - Re-run https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45284731868 — **success**. Command: `cargo +1.99.1 test --manifest-path pkgs/atlas-search/Cargo.toml -p atlas-core --lib attestation` - `test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 176 filtered out` — all 8 `attestation::tests` pass (round-trip + digest-is-sha256, key-reorder stability, non-canonical refusal, rejected-batch seal, prior-attestation chain, unsigned v1 envelope, fail-closed validation, proptest round-trip over generated rows). - `rustfmt --check` clean on the new file; `check-rust-module-reach.sh` reports no unreached atlas-core file (16 pre-existing unreached files are in pkgs/id, untouched here). ## Merge Danger Low. One new module + one `pub mod` line; no existing type, table, or gate behavior changes. The statement type is additive and consumed by nothing yet — the next slice (registry table + gate emission, then #11183 projector mapping) is what wires it in. ## Next slice After this PR, the `ingest_attestations` registry table + gate emission points (#6045 §3–§4) can land, and then #11183's projector emits `attestation.claim` + `atlas.wasGeneratedBy`, after which the attested-only preset itself lands on #13766. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-23T23:12:39Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "htch-runtime", "worktree": "/home/hatch", "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": { "kind": "worktree", "id": "/home/hatch", "repo": "developing-today/code", "branch": "main", "sha": "bbfc8aa3a3b4f3e3d399b7e76beb6962c0daa5b9" }, "auth_subject": "xaltha", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(aggregator): record-claude-launch refuses a flag token as an option value (#3415)
items.body: Fixes #3415 (task 6045; triaged CONFIRMED by task 5265). ## What `record-claude-launch.ts` read every value-taking option through `arg()`, which returned the next argv token unchecked. A flag token was accepted as the previous flag's value and then consumed again as a flag: `--task --model gpt-x` appended a record with `taskRefs: ["--model"]` and `model: "gpt-x"`; `--label --id claude-x` registered a session named `--id` — all with exit 0. - `arg()` and the `--task` collection now go through `valueAfter()`: a missing token or one starting with `--` is refused with a usage error (exit 2, matching the existing `--label is required` exit code) **before** any record is appended. - One token can never serve as both value and flag; control behaviour is unchanged, including repeated `--task` collecting multiple refs. ## Tests New pinning test `test/record-claude-launch-flag-value-3415.test.ts` (same Bun.spawn pattern as the #3295 fix): - flag-as-value for `--task`, `--label`, `--model`; a value flag in last position; bare `--label` — all exit 2 with the usage error and append nothing. - Control: normal invocation records exactly the given label, id, model, and both task refs. ### Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync`
[GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.
